item.title: Delta-Neutral Stablecoin Yield: Who Pays You, and When It Flips
item.description:
Fifteen percent on dollars, fully hedged, no price risk. What could go wrong? Mark walks Jules and Mira through the three failure modes that turn delta-neutral stablecoin yield into real losses, and Jules explains it all with a fantasy football pot that got repossessed.

Read the full article: Delta-Neutral Stablecoin Yields: When 15% APY Turns Into -20% Losses

With Mark, our regular on lending, bitcoin, stablecoins tron, liquidity lp, integrations, multichain, regulation macro, markets data, education basics, company.

In this episode

  • How a delta-neutral vault works: long spot, short perps, collect funding from leveraged longs
  • Why funding rates invert in bear markets (nearly -7% on a 30-day sum on Binance after late 2022)
  • How exchange counterparty risk can zero a perfectly hedged position, as FTX showed
  • Why liquidation cascades like October 10, 2025 ($9.89B liquidated, 70% in 40 minutes) break the hedge, and how Stream Finance's xUSD depegged over 77%
  • Four questions to ask before depositing, and why swap-fee yield is a different tradeoff

01:34 Failure mode one: funding flips negative
02:32 Failure mode two: Travis and the glovebox

item.title: Bitcoin-Backed Loans Without KYC, Click by Click (Plus Boost Yield)
item.description:

Today, he and Mira walk through the opposite experience: borrowing stablecoins against native BTC with no KYC, no custodian, and collateral that can now earn Boost fees while your loan is open.

item.title: Hardware Wallet Cross-Chain Swaps: Trading Straight From Cold Storage
item.description:
Hardware wallet users used to face a choice: keep keys in cold storage, or wrap their coins and trust a bridge to go anywhere. Jules's summer as a valet, and the night the key board fell off the wall, explains why wrapped tokens are just a ticket. Mark breaks down how Tangem and SwapKit route native swaps through Chainflip, and why the trades keep getting bigger.

Read the full article: Tangem and SwapKit Bring Hardware Wallet Users to Chainflip for Native Cross-Chain Swaps

With Mark, our regular on lending, bitcoin, stablecoins tron, liquidity lp, integrations, multichain, regulation macro, markets data, education basics, company.

In this episode

  • How a Tangem card wallet, SwapKit's routing layer and Chainflip fit together, without ever leaving the wallet app
  • Why native BTC-to-ETH settlement matters and why wBTC is a claim, not bitcoin
  • What actually happens at the Chainflip deposit address: a distributed validator set, consensus, and a custody window measured in minutes
  • Why larger swaps (with $2M+ single swaps expected) can get tighter pricing through JIT liquidity
  • Which chains and assets Tangem users can swap natively, from BTC to USDT on Tron

item.title: BTCFi Yield Risk, Ranked: Which Bitcoin Yield Bites Back?
item.description:
A guy at a wedding swears he gets 20% on his bitcoin 'from the app.' Mark joins Jules and Mira to rank BTCFi yield by what can actually go wrong: exploits, slashing, liquidation and impermanent loss. Bonus: Jules explains impermanent loss with a baseball card trade binder from a VFW swap meet.

Read the full article: BTCFi Yield Stack Ranked by Real Risk: Staking, Lending, LPing, and Swap-Fee Returns Compared

With Mark, our regular on lending, bitcoin, stablecoins tron, liquidity lp, integrations, multichain, regulation macro, markets data, education basics, company.

In this episode

  • The three-part risk framework: smart contract risk, return volatility and structural risk
  • Why Babylon staking's 1-3% APY is paid in protocol tokens, not BTC, and comes with slashing risk
  • Lending's $526M in exploits across 48 incidents, and how native BTC collateral removes bridge risk
  • Why over half of Uniswap V3 LPs in volatile pairs saw 11-17% annual impermanent loss

item.title: USDT on BNB Chain: Same Dollar, Cheaper Rails, One Big Gotcha
item.description:
Same Tether, different rails, wildly different fees. Jules tells the story of the two Elm Streets and the pizza he delivered to the wrong one, which turns out to be exactly how people lose USDT by picking the wrong network. Mira breaks down BEP-20 fees, the BNB gas rule, and how to swap to native BTC.

Read the full article: USDT on BNB Chain: A Beginner's Guide to BEP-20 Tether

In this episode

  • USDT-BEP20 is the same 1:1 dollar-pegged Tether, just settling on BNB Chain instead of Ethereum, Tron or Solana
  • BNB Chain's median fee was about $0.0038 in Q1 2026, versus several dollars for ERC-20 transfers on a busy Ethereum mainnet
  • You always need a little BNB for gas; if it hits zero, your USDT is stuck
  • BNB Chain uses the same 0x address format as Ethereum, so sending USDT-ERC20 to it without bridging loses funds: always check the network
  • Chainflip plans native swaps from USDT on BNB Chain to BTC, ETH, SOL and more in October 2026, with a flat 0.10% protocol fee plus network fees

item.title: Chainflip LP Returns: How to Read APY Without Getting Fooled
item.description:
Jules once made $800 in a day at a fireworks tent, multiplied it by 365, and told his mom he might skip school. That is exactly how people misread LP yield. Mark joins to explain where Chainflip LP returns really come from, which pools earn what, and how to check the numbers yourself instead of trusting a headline APY.

Read the full article: LP Returns, Measured: Where to find Fees, Volume, and APY on Chainflip Right Now

With Mark, our regular on lending, bitcoin, stablecoins tron, liquidity lp, integrations, multichain, regulation macro, markets data, education basics, company.

In this episode

  • All Chainflip LP yield comes from real swap fees, not token emissions: no swaps, no earnings.
  • JIT LPs compete to fill swaps and carry inventory risk; Boost LPs hold single-sided BTC with no impermanent loss and earn steadier, usually lower returns.
  • BTC pools have the highest absolute fee volume but the toughest competition; SOL market-making competition is currently lighter; stablecoin pools are high volume with tight spreads.
  • Use 24-hour data to see current activity, but judge sustainable returns on 7-day and 30-day rolling totals in Chainflip Scan.
  • APY moves with swap volume (including aggregator integrations like Rango and LI.FI), LP competition, and asset volatility.

item.title: BTC Loan Health Factor Zones: When to Add Collateral or Repay
item.description:
Your BTC loan was safe when you opened it. That doesn't mean it's safe now. Mark walks through the three numbers that decide whether you keep your collateral, the exact health factor where you should stop hoping and start acting, and why Jules's cousin Derek should never have driven on March ice.

Read the full article: Health Factor, LTV, and Liquidation Price: A BTC Borrower's Risk Playbook for Volatile Markets

With Mark, our regular on lending, bitcoin, stablecoins tron, liquidity lp, integrations, multichain, regulation macro, markets data, education basics, company.

item.title: Boost Yield Explained: Who's Actually Paying Your APY?
item.description:
A 500% APY sounds amazing until the token you're paid in drops 95%. Jules tells the story of the summer job that paid him in points that kept getting printed, and Mira breaks down why yield paid from real swap fees works differently from yield paid from a token printer. By the end you'll have one question to ask about any APY you see.

Read the full article: Where Does Boost Yield Actually Come From: Fee-Backed APY vs Emissions-Funded APY

In this episode

  • Boost LPs earn a 0.05% fee, paid in the native asset (BTC in, BTC out), for fronting deposits while validators confirm
  • Emissions-funded APY pays LPs in newly minted tokens, so supply rises, price falls and dollar returns shrink even when the percentage looks huge
  • SushiSwap's TVL fell 94% from $7.9B to $0.5B, and LPs who earned 500% APY in SUSHI saw those tokens lose 95% of their value
  • Fee-backed yield grows with usage, while emissions yield drops as emissions slow, no matter how much the protocol is used
  • The sustainability test: can this yield continue at current levels indefinitely, and who is actually paying it?

item.title: Multi-Hop Crypto Swaps: Why Three Legs Can Beat the Direct Route
item.description:
There's no single protocol that takes you from SOL to AVAX, so how does your swap get there? Mark breaks down how Rango chains Jupiter, Chainflip and other bridges into one route, and why the scenic route often pays better than the direct one. Plus: Jules's legendary Tuesday bus.

Read the full article: Rango Exchange Multi-Hop Swaps: How Chainflip Powers Cross-Chain Routing Segments

With Mark, our regular on lending, bitcoin, stablecoins tron, liquidity lp, integrations, multichain, regulation macro, markets data, education basics, company.

In this episode

  • A multi-hop swap splits one trade into ordered legs, each handled by the protocol best suited to that leg
  • Real routes: SOL to AVAX in three hops, MATIC to native BTC and DOT to SOL in two, with Chainflip handling the native cross-chain leg
  • Rango scores each leg on expected output, gas costs, execution time and reliability using live quotes
  • Multi-hop can beat a direct route through a thin pool, but single-hop Chainflip routes like native BTC to USDT still win when both sides are supported
  • Check route details before executing: if a middle hop fails you may end up holding the intermediate asset

item.title: Cross-Chain Arbitrage Math: Why That Price Gap Isn't Free Money
item.description:
ETH is $4 cheaper on Arbitrum than on Ethereum, so that's free money, right? Mark joins Jules and Mira to run the real numbers on cross-chain arbitrage, including a full-bitcoin trade that nets just $40.75. Leave with one formula that tells you whether any spread is actually worth taking.

Read the full article: How to Calculate If a Cross-Chain Arbitrage Trade Is Actually Profitable

With Mark, our regular on lending, bitcoin, stablecoins tron, liquidity lp, integrations, multichain, regulation macro, markets data, education basics, company.

In this episode

  • The three cost layers on every cross-chain arb: protocol fee (0.10% on Chainflip), gas on both chains, and slippage
  • A worked BTC vs cbBTC trade where a 0.22% spread on 1 BTC nets only $40.75, and a 0.15% spread loses money
  • The breakeven formula: protocol fee % + expected slippage % + (gas / trade size)
  • Why pros target 0.25%+ spreads and pass on anything under 1.5x breakeven
  • Where spreads show up: volatility, chain events, small stablecoin depegs, new listings and new chain integrations like Tron and BNB Chain

item.description:
Why do you need a different gas token for every chain you touch? Mark joins Jules and Mira to break down chain abstraction, the new UX bar where you say what you want instead of which chain. Plus: a car wash analogy that, against all odds, actually holds up.

With Mark, our regular on lending, bitcoin, stablecoins tron, liquidity lp, integrations, multichain, regulation macro, markets data, education basics, company.

In this episode

  • Chain abstraction hides the chain from the user while still settling natively, with no wrapped or custodial shortcuts
  • Account abstraction (ERC-4337) improves single-chain UX, with 26M+ smart accounts and 99.2% of UserOperations paymaster-funded, but doesn't cover cross-chain moves like ETH to BTC
  • Chainflip's deposit addresses let you swap by simply sending funds from any wallet, including cold storage and exchange withdrawals, with no wallet connection
  • Destination gas is paid by the protocol from swap proceeds, so you never need SOL or TRX to receive SOL or USDT
  • The new bar: no destination gas, any source address, native settlement, and one transaction regardless of chains
